Maya: Quick flag — rc3-quant bringup results on Holdout-A look odd: NDCG@10 drops ~2.1% but MRR@10 increases slightly. Running on same candidate set. Anyone seen flip like this?
Jorge: Can you paste the metric table and quant config? Which quant backend (q4/q8/hybrid)?
Maya: q4_0 w/ KV-cache enabled. Here's the summary:
```
model        NDCG@10  MRR@10
ranker-f32   0.412    0.224
ranker-q4    0.403    0.226
ranker-q8    0.409    0.229
```
Liam: Interesting — MRR up while NDCG down suggests top-1 swaps that help average reciprocal rank but hurt graded relevance ordering. Could be candidate scoring tie-break differences. :thinking_face:
Sophia: Also check candidate shard assignment and deterministic ordering. We had a bug that permuted long-doc candidates across shards during offline generation.
Maya: Good call — I reran a sample diff between f32 and q4 for 100 queries: 12 queries had top1 change where new top1 had lower relevance label. Command I used:
```bash
python tools/compare_scores.py --left scores_f32.json --right scores_q4.json --topk 1 --out diffs.csv
```
Jorge: Can you paste a tiny sample CSV inline? Also confirm seeding and any shuffling in candidate generation.
Maya: uploaded sample rows: (query_id, top1_f32, top1_q4, label_f32, label_q4) e.g., 12345,docA,docB,2,1 — seed & generation were same artifact id commit abc123.
ci-bot: deploy/rc3 to staging finished — 12 GPUs, kv-cache enabled. :white_check_mark:
Liam: Next steps I propose: 1) run determinism check (seed fixed) 2) diff candidate order pre-sort vs post-shard 3) run bipartite scoring comparison (float path vs quant path) 4) check label distribution on flipped queries. Can someone own 2 and 4?
Sophia: I'll take 2 (candidate ordering).
Jorge: I'll take 4 (label inspect) — will post sample analysis later today.
Maya: Thanks — filing issue #TICKET-987 for tracking. If we confirm ordering bug then revert or patch ledgering before promoting. :memo:
